patch.rationale: The bug in the function sum_first_n(n) is that the range function in Python is exclusive of the end value. Therefore, when calculating the sum of the integers 1..n inclusive, the range should be from 1 to n+1 to include n in the sum.
The bug in the average function is due to the use of integer division (//) which truncates the decimal part. To fix this, we should use floating point division (/) instead.

The issue arises from the mutable default argument in Python, which is only evaluated once at function definition time. To fix this, we use None as the default argument and initialize the list inside the function.
